title: README and GitHub CI workflow
description: Feature root for two tasks: (1) bootstrap README.md with user-facing docs and APM installation instructions, (2) create .github/workflows/test.yml that runs the test suite and creates a version tag on success.

handoff_summary.completed: Reviewed repo structure, confirmed neither README.md nor .github/ directory exist. Validated both pre-created child beads are correctly scoped. Enriched plan with acceptance criteria, expected files, and conflict risk assessment. Proposed shared review bead.
handoff_summary.remaining: Implementation by B-618cbc46 (README.md) and B-606890e7 (.github/workflows/test.yml), then review by the shared review bead.
handoff_summary.risks: The CI workflow bootstrap step (running `python memory.py --help` to trigger venv creation) must happen before pytest. If the ONNX model download fails in CI, tests requiring embeddings will fail — but tests mock `_embed()` by default so this should be safe. sqlite-vec may require a specific ubuntu runner version.
handoff_summary.next_action: Schedule B-618cbc46 and B-606890e7 in parallel (no file overlap). Once both complete, run shared review bead.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: B-618cbc46 touches only README.md; B-606890e7 touches only .github/workflows/test.yml. Neither overlaps with any active bead (B-b082bd73-docs touches memory.py only). Safe to run in parallel.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: CI workflow uses two jobs in one file (test + tag) consistent with the sister-project template provided in B-606890e7. Bootstrap via `python memory.py --help` triggers venv creation before pytest. Version tag bumps patch from latest vX.Y.Z (starts v0.1.0 if no tags). README targets two audiences: users (APM install, day-to-day usage) and developers (repo layout, test running).
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No new test files needed. Existing test suite in tests/ and test_commands.py covers memory.py behavior. CI workflow will run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ test_commands.py`.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: APM install URL in README will use a placeholder github.com URL since the actual published repo URL is unknown at planning time. Developer implementing B-618cbc46 should use the actual repo URL if available, or a `<repo-url>` placeholder otherwise.

conflict_risks: B-618cbc46 touches only README.md; B-606890e7 touches only .github/workflows/test.yml. Neither overlaps with any active bead (B-b082bd73-docs touches memory.py only). Safe to run in parallel.

execution_history.summary: Decomposed B-33389719 into two existing implementation beads (B-618cbc46 for README.md, B-606890e7 for CI workflow) plus one new shared review bead. Both implementation beads are independent, touch different files, and can run in parallel.

guardrails.template_text:
# Planner Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Decompose a feature into a parent epic and actionable child beads with clear dependencies and scope.

Allowed actions:
- Read specifications and repository context.
- Propose bead structure, dependencies, linked docs, and expected file scope.
- Create follow-up planning work when decomposition is blocked by missing information.

Disallowed actions:
- Implement code, tests, docs, or runtime behavior changes.
- Claim work outside planning scope as completed.

Expected outputs:
- Structured planning JSON matching the planner schema.
- Beads with concise, role-appropriate acceptance criteria and file scope.

Developer bead sizing:
- Plan developer beads as a single focused change that should fit within roughly 10 minutes of implementation work.
- Split broader logical units into dependent developer beads instead of assigning one bead to absorb multiple distinct changes.
- If a change is likely to touch more than 2-3 functions, span multiple subsystems, or mix unrelated refactors with feature work, break it into smaller dependent beads with explicit ordering.

Shared follow-up beads:
- For features with multiple related implementation beads, create shared tester, documentation, and review beads instead of duplicating that work inside each developer bead.
- The shared tester bead should depend on the relevant implementation beads it validates.
- The shared documentation bead should depend on the validated implementation set when docs need to describe the combined result.
- The shared review bead should depend on the validated implementation set so review happens after the combined changes are ready.
